title: Artifact Engine Demo
description: A 2-minute demonstration of how the Artifact Engine automatically captures, analyzes, and organizes developer work through screenshots and git commits.

scenes.title: The Problem
scenes.description: Opening scene showing scattered developer work - desktop with random screenshots, terminal windows, and git commits that get lost over time.
scenes.narration: Every week, I take dozens of screenshots and make hundreds of git commits. By Friday, it's all scattered and forgotten. What if none of that work ever disappeared again?
scenes.notes: Show messy desktop with scattered screenshots and terminal windows

scenes.title: Taking a Screenshot
scenes.description: Demonstration of taking a normal screenshot of code or terminal output, showing the natural workflow.
scenes.narration: Watch this. I take a screenshot like normal...
scenes.notes: Actually take a screenshot of code/terminal in real-time

scenes.title: AI Processing
scenes.description: The screenshot being automatically processed by the AI system, showing the analysis in progress.
scenes.narration: The AI immediately analyzes it, determines it's code-related, generates a descriptive title, writes a technical summary, and files it automatically in this week's folder.
scenes.notes: Show processing notification, then navigate to generated file

scenes.title: Generated Artifact
scenes.description: The final organized result - a well-structured markdown file with AI-generated insights, properly categorized and timestamped.
scenes.narration: Look at that - it understood the context, extracted the key technical details, and created a timestamp-prefixed file so nothing ever gets overwritten. All automatic, zero manual work.
scenes.notes: Show the generated markdown with AI analysis and weekly folder structure

scenes.title: Making a Git Commit
scenes.description: Demonstration of making a normal git commit, showing the standard developer workflow.
scenes.narration: Same thing happens with commits. I make a normal git commit...
scenes.notes: Actually make a git commit in real-time

scenes.title: Commit Analysis
scenes.description: The commit being automatically analyzed, showing the system capturing the diff and generating documentation.
scenes.narration: The system captures the diff, analyzes what changed, categorizes the work, and generates documentation with links back to the actual commit. It even maintains context across the week's work.
scenes.notes: Show commit processing and generated commit artifact

scenes.title: Commit Documentation
scenes.description: The rich documentation generated from the commit, showing technical insights and connections to other work.
scenes.narration: Now I have rich documentation of what I built, why it matters, and how it connects to my other work - all generated from my normal workflow.
scenes.notes: Show generated commit documentation with links and context

scenes.title: The Compound Result
scenes.description: Final view of the organized weekly knowledge base, showing multiple artifacts working together to create a comprehensive record.
scenes.narration: After just one week, I have a structured knowledge base of everything I accomplished. My work compounds automatically, and I never lose another breakthrough.
scenes.notes: Show weekly folder with multiple organized artifacts and end card

callToAction: Artifact Engine - Your work, automatically documented
